column1: # Board results sw55-sw58, 2026-09-11. Backfilled from each run's own transcript segment.
# Bitstream for every row: caplifive_r25r26r27_66c4e7517.bit (RTL 66c4e7517). No flash between them.
# WHY THIS FILE WAS EMPTY FOR THESE BOOTS. The close-out rule is that readings land here WITH the
# image hash, because a row's LABEL can name a different program -- that is R-29, found by a value
# sitting outside its reproducer's documented range. These four boots were written up in
# ref/fpga-silicon-measurements-for-paper.md SS7h-SS7k and never reached the corpus.
# HOW THESE ROWS WERE EXTRACTED, and what that does and does not guarantee: each transcript was
# scoped to its OWN load_image before anything was read, because the console replays the previous
# boot on connect. Domain and baseline arms are told apart by the marker that FOLLOWS the cycle
# count -- the baseline binary emits SPEEDTEST1-CYCLES too, so counting that marker alone
# over-reports the domain arms by the number of baseline arms.
# The image hash column is the DOMAIN image for domain rows and the baseline binary for baseline
# rows. Columns with no value in the transcript are 'n/a' rather than guessed: the domain arms of
# sw56 carry no instruction count at all (that is why sw57 was run), and bigregion rows have no
# IMAGE HASHES ARE CROSS-CHECKED, not taken from the current working copy on trust. bigregion.user
# hashes identically (9d18522bd95579a9, 19032 B) in the live overlay and in the two copies stashed
# independently by the sw56 and sw57 retire/restore steps, so the file the rows cite is the file
# sw55 ran. That check exists because a hash column taken from whatever happens to be on disk today
# would reintroduce exactly the defect it is here to prevent.
# Row counts, each matching what the boot ran: sw55 4 (control + three CMA sizes), sw56 15 (control
# + 7 pairs), sw57 8 (control + 7 instrumented), sw58 16 (control + 7 pairs + main repeated last as
# cols: label  entryVA  opt  region  image16  retval  boot  pos  status  value  cycles  note
